title: Every retry button says exactly "Try again", plus three fixes you approved

steps.path: Marketplace → Integrations → Google Workspace, after an install that failed
steps.headline: A failed install now says one short sentence with "Try again"; the technical reason waits under Details.
steps.changed: Was "Couldn't install: Plugin not found in marketplace: google-workspace …" beside "Try installing again". Now "Google Workspace couldn't be installed." with "Try again" inside the box, and the installer's own words in a Details fold under it — the shape you approved for Contribute's failures.
steps.notice: Plugin and theme pages use this same box, word for word (next slide).

steps.path: Marketplace → a plugin → Install, when the install fails
steps.headline: Plugin pages show the identical failed-install box, so all detail pages match.
steps.changed: "Couldn't download it: the source repository did not answer …" with "Try installing again" becomes "Browser Use couldn't be installed." with "Try again", and the reason under Details.
steps.notice: Same sentence pattern, same button, same Details fold as the integration page.

steps.path: The version pill → Update now, when the download fails
steps.headline: A failed update is a sentence in the notice box with "Try again", instead of "Download failed — Try again" on the button.
steps.changed: The failure lived in the big button's label ("Download failed — Try again"), with "Open in browser instead" under it. Now the notice box takes the button's place: "The update didn't download.", then "Open in browser instead" and "Try again" inside it.
steps.notice: Other failures read the same way: "The installer didn't start.", "The download was damaged, so it wasn't installed." (no browser option there — that file is the one the check refused).

steps.path: Backup & sync, when a Google Drive backup timed out
steps.headline: Backup & sync's fix buttons read "Try again", not "Try again now".
steps.changed: Every Backup & sync warning that offers a retry (timed out, disk full, couldn't connect, too many uploads, and the rest) now labels its button "Try again".
steps.notice: A small test now checks the whole app, phone included, so a variant can't come back.

steps.surface: Settings → Backup & sync → Add a backup
steps.headline: On a computer, Add a backup no longer offers GitHub, which had copied nothing since its backup was removed.
steps.changed: The picker offered Google Drive and GitHub. A GitHub backup made here saved its settings but nothing ever copied to it. Now only the choices that work are offered (Google Drive; iCloud too on Mac and Windows).
steps.notice: Your files sync to GitHub through cross-device sync, at the top of Backup & sync — that is unchanged.

steps.path: Backup & sync, for someone who set up a GitHub backup earlier
steps.headline: A GitHub backup set up earlier now says it's no longer supported, with Remove, instead of a false "Backed up".
steps.changed: Its row read "Backed up 5m ago" with a green light, though nothing was copied. Now: "No longer supported", a grey light, and a warning notice inside its box saying nothing is copied and what's on GitHub stays — with Remove, which opens the usual Remove confirm. Its settings and files are never deleted on their own.
steps.notice: Same notice-inside-the-item look as Local models' interrupted download.

steps.path: Android, Backup & sync → Add a backup
steps.headline: The phone app still backs up to GitHub by itself. Should it keep offering the GitHub backup?
steps.today: On the phone app (not paired to a computer), a GitHub backup still really copies your memory and settings to a GitHub repository.
steps.problem: Computers no longer have it, so the two apps differ.
steps.proposal: For now the phone keeps the option, because there it works. Removing it there too would make the apps match, but take away a working backup from anyone using it.

options.label: Keep on phone
pros: Nothing that works is taken away
cons: The phone offers a choice computers don't

options.label: Remove everywhere
pros: Both apps offer the same choices
cons: Phone users lose a backup that works; theirs would show "no longer supported"

steps.surface: Settings → Backup & sync → Add a backup
steps.path: Add a backup → Google Drive → Connect to Google, when the sign-in fails
steps.headline: A failed sign-in now shows the sign-in's real reason with Try again, not a cheerful guess.
steps.changed: It always said "Looks like the sign-in didn't complete. No worries — try again when you're ready." and dropped the actual reason, with Try again below the main button. Now the reason the sign-in gave sits in the error box with Try again inside it, in the button's place; when there is no reason, only "The sign-in didn't finish."
steps.notice: The practice reason here is made up; the real app shows Google's or GitHub's own words.

steps.headline: "Runs fast — fits on your GPU" is now a green-tinted pill with normal words, not green text.
steps.changed: How well a model fits was coloured words: green "Runs fast — fits on your GPU", amber "Will be tight…", red "Too large for this machine". Now the same words sit in a status pill in that colour, like the Local engine's Running / Stopped pill above it.
steps.notice: Same words and colours, just in the pill's tint — the guide's rule that status colours never colour the words.

steps.surface: Choosing a model for a conversation
steps.path: The model menu, when a local model may not fit in memory
steps.headline: Found nearby: the model menu's "may not fit in memory" warning is amber or red text. Fix it the same way next round?
steps.today: When you pick a local model that may not fit, the model menu shows a fold titled "This model may not fit in available memory" in amber (red when too large).
steps.problem: That is status colour in text, which the guide rules out. It isn't on Local models itself, so it wasn't changed here.
steps.proposal: Next round, make it the warning notice box — tinted box, normal words — keeping its fold and the "Warn me about this model" switch inside.
